chunks: Ali ibn Muhammad ibn Bundar, from Ibrahim ibn Is'haq al-Ahmar, from Abdullah ibn Hammad, from Abu Maryam al-Ansari, from Abu Barza al-Aslami who said:
A child was born to al-Hasan ibn Ali (peace be upon him), and the Quraysh came to him and said: 'Congratulations for the horse-rider!'

So he said: 'And what is this as a saying? Say instead: May you have thanked the Endower, and may blessing be upon you in the endowed (child), and may God bring him to his full maturity, and grant you (to witness) his righteousness.'

key_terms.أَشُدَّهُ: Full maturity/prime — the age of complete physical and mental strength, often associated with religious responsibility
key_terms.الْفَارِسُ: Horse-rider/cavalier — a pre-Islamic congratulatory term implying the newborn will become a warrior/hero; the Imam's rejection of this phrase signals a break from tribal values
key_terms.الْمَوْهُوبِ: The endowed/gifted one — referring to the newborn as a blessing granted by God
key_terms.الْوَاهِبَ: The Endower/Bestower — a name/attribute of God emphasizing that children are a divine gift
key_terms.بِرَّهُ: His righteousness/filial piety — the virtuous conduct of the child toward his parents and God

ai.seo_question: What is the Islamic congratulations for a newborn according to Imam al-Hasan?
ai.summary: When a son was born to Imam al-Hasan ibn Ali (AS), Arab visitors from Quraysh congratulated him with the pre-Islamic phrase wishing for a horse-rider (warrior), reflecting tribal culture's valorization of military prowess. The Imam corrected this by teaching the proper Islamic congratulatory supplication that focuses on gratitude to God, blessings in the child, hoping the child reaches adulthood, and praying for the parents to benefit from the child's righteousness. This hadith establishes the Sunnah of the Imams on newborn congratulations — shifting focus from worldly ambitions to spiritual gratitude and piety.

en.hubeali: Ali Bin Muhammad Bin Bundar, from Ibrahim Bin Is’haq Al Ahmar, from Abdullah Bin Hammad, from Abu Maryam Al Ansary, from Abu Barzat Al Aslamy who said,

‘A child was born for Ali<sup>asws</sup> Bin Al-Husayn<sup>asws</sup>, so the Qureysh came over to him<sup>asws</sup> and said, ‘Congratulations to you<sup>asws</sup> for the (birth of a) horse-rider’.

So he<sup>asws</sup> said: ‘And what is this from the speech? You should be saying, ‘Thank the Endower, Blessings be to you<sup>asws</sup> regarding the endowed, and may Allah<sup>azwj</sup> Make him reach the adulthood, and Grant you<sup>asws</sup> (to observe) his righteousness’.
en.sarwar: 2. Ali ibn Muhammad ibn Bandar has narrated from Ibrahim ibn Ishaq al-Ahmar from ‘Abd Allah ibn Hammad from abu Maryam al- Ansariy from abu Barzah al-Aslamiy who has said the following:
“A child was born to al-Husayn ibn Ali, ‘Alayhi al-Salam, and Quraysh came to congratulate him (the Imam) and said, ‘Congratulations to you for the birth of the rider (the knight).’

He (the Imam) said, ‘What kind of expression is this! Say, “May Allah enable you to thank the Benefactor for the blessed gift, may Allah make him to grow up to manhood and may Allah give you the chance to enjoy his good deeds!”’
